result.note: Tests the MoRTH draft amendment for E85/E100, the E20 rollout and feedstock mix, and fuel facts including the NITI Aayog pricing advice.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the draft rules on higher ethanol blends published in April 2026:
items: The draft was published by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
It proposes amending the Central Motor Vehicles Rules to add E85 and E100 fuels to India's regulatory framework.
The draft is open for public comment for 30 days.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. MoRTH proposed amending the Central Motor Vehicles Rules to recognise E85 and E100 and opened the draft to 30 days of public comment. The amendment creates a legal basis for type-approval testing of vehicles built for higher blends, with a phased E85 rollout targeted for late 2026.
questions.source: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) proposed amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules adding E85 (85% ethanol, 15% petrol) and E100 (nearly pure ethanol) to India's regulatory framework.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's ethanol blending programme as of April 2026:
items: Grain-based ethanol accounts for a majority of India's ethanol production.
The mandatory nationwide rollout of E20 on 1 April 2026 came a year later than the original target.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because India achieved the E20 rollout a year ahead of its original target, not behind it. Grain-based ethanol now makes up 60% of production, though sugarcane remains the crop that shapes politics.
questions.source: This follows the mandatory nationwide rollout of E20 (20% ethanol) on 1 April 2026, which India achieved a year ahead of its original target.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to ethanol-blended fuels:
items: Energy content of ethanol — roughly 27-30% less per litre than petrol
NITI Aayog recommendation of 2021 — higher-blend fuels to be priced above regular petrol
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The third pair is wrong. In 2021 NITI Aayog recommended pricing higher-blend fuels below regular petrol to compensate for their lower energy content, and this has not been implemented for E20. Running on E85 or E100 needs a flex-fuel vehicle, and no mass-market model is sold in India.
questions.source: NITI Aayog, India’s apex public policy think tank, recommended in 2021 that higher-blend fuels be priced below regular petrol to compensate for the energy loss.
